transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump says he wants former Apple CEO Tim Cook to be the CEO of Nvidia
after the resignation of Jensen Wong.
Wong has been close to Trump and traveled with him to China as a White House-considered AI policy.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben has more.
On social media, Trump wrote that Wong has done, quote, "a fantastic job."
He added, quote, "There is only one man to take his place, Tim Cook of Apple.
A legend replaces a legend."
Wong announced his resignation after news reports alleging
that he had had an extramarital affair with one of the company's clients,
who U.S. intelligence officials concluded had been recruited by China's top spy agency.
Wong has had the President's ear for much of this term,
demonstrated in September when Trump called Wong's phone
while Wong was on stage at a conference.
He also joined Trump on a state visit to the U.K. last year and to China this year.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News, The White House.
Nvidia's board has appointed Collette Kress as interim CEO.
Kress joined the company in 2013, serving as executive vice president and chief financial officer.
The federal government's new fiscal year, starting out much like the old one deep in the red,
NPR's Scott Horsley reports on the government's more than $400 billion deficit in the month of October.
Setting aside some calendar quirks, government tax receipts were down 6 percent in October,
compared to a year ago, while government spending was up by 12 percent.
Some of that spending increase just reflects a return to normal operations,
compared to October 2025 when the government was shut down.
The Agriculture Department also spent an extra $14 billion last month,
with much of that going to help farmers who were hard hit by the president's trade policies
and the high costs associated with the war with Iran.
In addition, the government paid $115 billion in interest last month,
an 11 percent increase from October of 2025.
Borrowing costs have been climbing as a result of higher interest rates
and the government's ballooning debt.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
A widespread Microsoft service outage impacted thousands of users Thursday.
The tech giant, based in Washington state, says it's working to get affected service back in servers.
The outage caused some businesses to close for the day,
as Anna Marie Yanny of memberatation KNKX reports.
Outlook emails, Microsoft Teams messaging, and other 365 services were affected.
Gary Renville runs the nonprofit Project Access Northwest.
His small team connects low-income patients with health and dental care.
We actually had to shut down our business because of the outage.
I had to send my employees home.
He says without Teams and Outlook, they didn't have a secure way to talk to patients.
Microsoft spent much of the day working on the outage,
saying they were pursuing "all available pathways to restore service."
For NPR News, I'm Anna Marie Yanny in Seattle.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The Kennedy Center says it plans to move ticketing over to Ticketmaster.
An NPR investigation, though, has found that the center's former president,
Richard Grinnell, was a paid board member of Ticketmaster's para company
at the time of the negotiations.
NPR's Anastasia Siolkas reports.
Richard Grinnell was appointed as the key center's president in February 2025,
just as President Trump became the institution's chairman.
A few months later, Grinnell was appointed to the board of Ticketmaster's parent company,
Live Nation, for which he was paid over $260,000.
Critics say this raises conflict of interest concerns.
Both Ticketmaster and the Kennedy Center say their discussions predated Grinnell's dual appointments,
but current and former senior Kennedy Center staffers, who asked for anonymity due to fears
of retribution, say Ticketmaster was never under serious consideration by senior staff
until Grinnell's tenure.
The Kennedy Center's main theaters remain closed.
The annual Kennedy Center honors are scheduled to take place December 7 at
Washington's Capital One Arena.
Anastasia Siolkas, NPR News.
President Trump's son, Donald Trump Jr., is no longer a paid advisor for the Kowsi
prediction market.
Kowsi said Thursday that the decision was mutual, following a decision by Trump Jr.'s
investment firm to increase its investment in polymarket, Kowsi's biggest competitor.
The announcement came after Democrats won control of Congress and last week's
midterm elections.
Democrats say they plan to investigate Trump family investments, including relationships
with both prediction markets.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump wants Tim Cook to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO after Huang's resignation
Nvidia board names Colette Kress interim CEO; she joined the company in 2013
Federal deficit exceeds $400 billion in October as tax receipts fall and spending rises
Widespread Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook and Teams, forcing some businesses to close
Kennedy Center plans to move ticketing to Ticketmaster; NPR finds former president Richard Grinnell was Live Nation board member
Donald Trump Jr. ends paid advisory role with prediction market Kalshi after investment in rival Polymarket
